summary: Eighteen of twenty checks pass and the ablation curve reproduces its own model exactly, but the ship runs out of fuel before circularising in all three bands and the cheapest descent is a single plunge at every band and load — the second of those is a rule no parameter assignment can satisfy and needs a human decision, not a retune.

checks.statement: Every band name used in the catalog or the params appears in the baseline's bands, and no undefined band is referenced.
checks.evidence: Baseline defines exactly {suborbital, low, high}. Catalog debris[].band uses {suborbital (9), low (9), high (10)} and band_summary uses the same three. Params reference the same three keys in ablation.heat_index, ablation.cost_curve, ablation.optimal_skims and economy.band_value_multiplier. Set difference in both directions is empty. armstrongs_satellite carries band 'high' although GDD 2.3.7 places it above the top band; that is bookkeeping placement against a name the baseline does define, not an undefined band.

checks.statement: Each band_summary entry agrees with the debris array it summarises on piece_count, mean_mass_kg and fragile_fraction.
checks.evidence: Suborbital: 9 pieces counted vs 9 claimed; masses 430+45+85+130+35+700+380+70+1100 = 2975, /9 = 330.56 vs 330.6 claimed; fragile spawn weights 5+3 = 8 over total 9+16+13+15+5+7+10+3+2 = 80, = 0.100 vs 0.1 claimed. Low: 9 vs 9; 870+760+390+1150+340+155+210+420+2000 = 6295, /9 = 699.44 vs 699.4; fragile weights 6+4+3 = 13 over 65 = 0.200 vs 0.2. High: 10 vs 10; 1950+1600+2200+1150+700+920+1300+540+3200+3600 = 17160, /10 = 1716.0 vs 1716; fragile weights 6+5+2+1 = 14 over 56 = 0.250 vs 0.25. Note the fractions are spawn-weighted, not by type count (by type they would be 0.222 / 0.333 / 0.400); the weighted reading is the one that matches, and it is the one the player meets.

checks.statement: Mean piece mass rises band over band, so valuable junk physically fights you.
checks.evidence: 330.56 -> 699.44 -> 1716.0 kg, steps of 2.12x and 2.45x, 5.19x end to end. Hand-tetherable only (excluding the oversized class the hand magnet cannot take): suborbital (2975-1100)/8 = 234.4, low (6295-2000)/8 = 536.9, high (17160-3200-3600)/8 = 1295.0 kg — 2.29x and 2.41x, 5.53x end to end. Monotonic under both readings.

checks.statement: Fragile spawn share rises across the bands, roughly 1 in 10 suborbital to 1 in 4 high.
checks.evidence: Spawn-weighted fragile share 8/80 = 0.100, 13/65 = 0.200, 14/56 = 0.250. Strictly increasing; the endpoints are exactly the 1-in-10 and 1-in-4 the GDD asks for.

checks.statement: A full hold roughly doubles the rocket's mass at starting storage size.
checks.evidence: cargo.base_slots 6 x the flown 232.96 kg per crushed slot = 1397.8 kg against dry_mass_kg 1350: (1350 + 1397.8) / 1350 = 2.035x. The simulator reports full_hold_mass_ratio 2.04 independently. Within 25% of doubling (window 1.75-2.25) with 0.21 of margin on one side and 0.29 on the other. Cross-check against the catalog rather than the sim: a six-slot suborbital hold under a tier-1 compactor (small crushed to 1 slot, medium uncrushed at 4) is bracketed by 749-984 kg, i.e. 1.55-1.73x, so the ratio is carried by the mixed shipping-slice loadout the sim flew, not by a suborbital-only run.

checks.statement: The skim cost curve's minimum sits at 1 or 2 skims in the high band, no band's optimum exceeds the high band's, each minimum equals its optimal_skims entry, and the curve is what the stated model produces.
checks.evidence: Model recomputed from params.ablation (base 0.28, growth 1.8, coeff 1.25e-5, exponent 3, skim_peak 22). High band, index 0: toll 0.28 + 1.25e-5*138^3 (2,628,072) = 0.28+32.851 = 33.131 vs 33.13. Index 2: tolls 0.28+0.504+0.9072 = 1.6912, skim heat 2*1.25e-5*10648 = 0.2662, entry 1.25e-5*(138*0.971 = 133.998)^3 = 1.25e-5*2,405,996 = 30.075, total 32.032 vs 32.03. Low index 0: 0.28+1.25e-5*1e6 = 12.78 vs 12.78; low index 3: 3.324+0.399+1.25e-5*95.8^3 (879,218 -> 10.990) = 14.713 vs 14.71. Suborbital index 0: 0.28+1.25e-5*474,552 = 6.212 vs 6.21; index 2: 1.6912+0.2662+1.25e-5*75.738^3 (434,451 -> 5.431) = 7.388 vs 7.39. Every recomputed point is inside 0.05%. Minima: suborbital index 0, low index 0, high index 2, matching optimal_skims {0,0,2} exactly; high's 2 is the maximum across bands and is inside the required 1-2. Judged on the curve, the model and the measured skim study only. Substituting the measured high-band array [1,0.99,0.98,0.972] into the same model gives 33.13 / 32.80 / 32.88 / 33.89, which moves the minimum to 1 skim — still inside 1-2, so the rule survives the measurement even though the stated optimal_skims.high value does not (routed under skim_multiplier_matches_measured and in observations).

checks.statement: The cheapest descent is 2-4 committed passes, never a single plunge and never feathering.
checks.evidence: Judged on flown pass counts only. descents[].cheapest_pass_count = 1 in all nine band x load cases. The series are monotonically increasing from the first pass in every one: suborbital empty 4.6 / 5.6 / 6.6 / 8.3 / 11.3 / 16.6 / 26.1 / 43.3%; low full hold 11.7 / 14.9 / 16.5 / 18.3 / 21.3 / 27.7%; high full hold 10.8 / 15.8 / 17.4 / 19.4 / 22.6 / 28.3%. The failure is a single plunge, not feathering. The reason is visible in the same tables: peak heat is almost flat in pass count because braking altitude climbs as passes are added — suborbital empty 70 -> 74 while braking altitude goes 27,846 -> 38,424 m; high full hold 94 -> 108 across 22,450 -> 30,221 m. A heat term that gives back 4-14 points of peak cannot pay for a cycle toll that compounds at 1.8x, so no assignment of cycle_toll_base_pct, cycle_toll_growth, heat_cost_coefficient or heat_cost_exponent moves the minimum off 1 — lowering the toll flattens the curve toward pass 1, raising the heat term steepens it toward pass 1. Inside a 43,000 m atmosphere at this ballistic coefficient the U-curve does not exist. This is not a value the Balancer chose badly; it is a rule the parameters cannot satisfy.
checks.fix_hint: No value in this file can pass this rule — do not tune toward it; the choice is the human's between substituting the skim framing into GDD 2.3.1 and taking the named GDD 4.5 risk-1 fallback of flat per-pass ablation with a hard pass cap.

checks.statement: The claimed skim_heat_multiplier matches what the simulator measured for the same quantity in the high band.
checks.evidence: Claimed [1, 0.985, 0.971, 0.958] against skims.high.skim_heat_multiplier_measured [1, 0.99, 0.98, 0.972], both taken at fixed entry depth. Entry-by-entry deltas 0.000 / 0.005 / 0.009 / 0.014 — the largest is 0.014, inside the 0.10 tolerance by 7x. The array is directionally right and slightly optimistic: it claims three skims buy 4.2% of peak heat where the sim measured 2.8%. That gap is small enough to pass this check but large enough to move the stated optimum (see the cost-curve evidence and observations), because the whole skim economy is priced off differences of a few hundredths of a plate-percent.

checks.statement: skim_heat_multiplier starts at 1.0, is non-increasing and flattens by its last two entries; cycle_toll_growth exceeds 1.
checks.evidence: [1, 0.985, 0.971, 0.958]: first entry exactly 1.0; successive deltas -0.015, -0.014, -0.013, so non-increasing and the last two steps differ by 0.001 — the benefit is saturating, not still falling. cycle_toll_growth 1.8 > 1, so the toll compounds (0.28, 0.504, 0.907, 1.633 per cycle) and an indefinite skim is bounded. The measured array [1, 0.99, 0.98, 0.972] saturates the same way (steps -0.010, -0.010, -0.008).

checks.statement: Parachute descent speed at full hold is under the soft-landing threshold but near enough that the Parachute upgrade is a real purchase.
checks.evidence: descent_speed_full_hold_ms 4.59 against soft_landing_ms 5.0 — inside the window 3.5-5.0, with 0.41 m/s of headroom (8.2% of the threshold). Flown touchdowns 3.22 / 3.96 / 4.59 m/s at empty / half / full hold, soft_landing true in all nine descents. Storage tier 1 (8 slots) puts the full hold at 1350 + 8*232.96 = 3213.7 kg and the speed at sqrt(2*3213.7*9/2349) = 4.96 m/s, one slot short of the hard-landing line, so Parachute tier 1 (1180 m2 -> 4.26 m/s) is a purchase the ladder actually forces.

checks.statement: The claimed full-hold descent speed is what the stated canopy actually flies, measured independently of the claim.
checks.evidence: params state parachute_area_m2 870 and parachute_drag_coefficient 1.8, so the measured block reports independent = true and the measurement is not solved backwards out of the claim. claimed_full_hold_ms 4.59, measured_full_hold_ms 4.59, delta_ms 0, spread_across_bands_ms 0 — against a 5% tolerance of 0.23 m/s. Recomputed here from the stated canopy and the flown mass: sqrt(2*2747.8*9.0 / (1.5*1.8*870)) = sqrt(49460.4/2349) = sqrt(21.056) = 4.589 m/s.

checks.statement: The tow fee is zero inside the free radius, linear beyond it, clamps at exactly 50% at half the planet's circumference, and can never go negative or exceed the cap.
checks.evidence: free_radius_m 1200, curve 'linear', max_fee_fraction 0.5 exactly. Half circumference = pi * 200,000 = 628,318.5 m. Fee(d) = 0.5 * (d - 1200) / (628,318.5 - 1200) = 0.5 * (d-1200)/627,118.5, clamped to [0, 0.5]: at d = 1200 it is 0, at d = 314,759 it is 0.2500, at d = 628,318.5 it is exactly 0.5000. Below 1200 m the numerator is negative and the clamp holds it at 0; beyond half the circumference there is nowhere further to land on a sphere, and the cap holds regardless. Payout therefore runs 100% at the pad and never below 50%. free_radius 1200 m as 'about one screen' is consistent with a 200 km-radius planet.

checks.statement: Launch cost is at or below the value of three cheap suborbital pieces.
checks.evidence: Three cheap suborbital pieces = 3 x size_class_base_value.small 40 x band_value_multiplier.suborbital 1.0 = 120. launch_cost 120, so the test is satisfied at equality (120 <= 120), the top of the GDD's stated two-to-three-piece window. Full lazy run: six crushed slots as four smalls and one medium sells for 4*40 + 90 = 250; costs are 120 for the stage plus a direct suborbital entry's flown 13.5% of plate at replate_cost_per_pct 3 = 40.5, total 160.5, clearing by 89.5. Using the Balancer's own 6.21% curve figure instead of the flown ablation the cost is 138.6 and it clears by 111.4; it breaks even under either.

checks.statement: Steady-state towing tension never reaches the magnet hold force, so shear can only fire on impulsive tension.
checks.evidence: a = jetpack_thrust_n / (suit_mass_kg + towed) and per-cable tension = m_piece * a. Heaviest legal two-piece hand-tetherable load is two cryo_propellant_sphere at 2200 kg: a = 240/(110+4400) = 0.0532 m/s2, tension = 2200*0.0532 = 117.1 N against magnet_hold_force_n 900 — 7.7x margin. Heaviest single piece: a = 240/(110+2200) = 0.1039, tension 228.6 N, 3.94x margin. Two battery_pack_module at 1150 kg: a = 240/2410 = 0.0996, tension 114.5 N. The general bound is tension = 240*m/(110+total) < jetpack_thrust_n = 240 N for every load and every tether count, so 900 N is never approached at base tier, still less at tiers 1 (1400 N) and 2 (2000 N).

checks.statement: No parameter reintroduces thrust after staging.
checks.evidence: The only thrust fields in the params are flight.thrust_n 78000 and flight.rcs_thrust_n 1900, both attached to the stage that staging jettisons, and eva.jetpack_thrust_n 240, which belongs to the astronaut and is the get-out-and-push allowance GDD 2.3.1 explicitly permits. No upgrade entry restores either ship thrust post-stage: the twelve entries touch fuel_capacity_kg, thrust_n, base_slots, plate_capacity_pct, parachute_area_m2 and magnet_hold_force_n only. There is no post-stage thrust, restart, reserve-tank or relight parameter anywhere in the file.

checks.statement: Fragile pieces are crushable at no compactor tier present in the params, and the fragile premium makes one intact fragile piece worth several solid pieces of the same class and band.
checks.evidence: cargo.compactor_tier 1 is the only tier in the params, and tier 1 crushes small only; no parameter grants any tier authority over the fragile flag, and the catalog carries fragile as a flag orthogonal to size_class rather than as a crushable class. fragile_value_premium 3.0: a suborbital fragile small is 40 x 1.0 x 3 = 120 against 40 for a solid small — three solid pieces of the same class and band, and it also costs 2 uncrushed slots against the solid piece's 1, so per slot it is 60 vs 40 (1.5x). A low-band fragile medium is 90 x 2.4 x 3 = 648 against 216 solid. 3x is at the low end of 'several' and the per-slot premium is only 1.5x once the uncrushable slot cost is charged; it passes but see observations.

checks.statement: Oversized junk rejects the hand magnet.
checks.evidence: size_classes.oversized.hand_tetherable = false, against true for small and medium. Slot costs match GDD 2.3.4 exactly: small 1/2, medium 2/4, oversized 6/12. The three oversized pieces (collapsed_launch_shroud 1100 kg, derelict_upper_stage_tank 2000 kg, high_gain_dish_assembly 3200 kg) plus armstrongs_satellite 3600 kg are therefore crane-cable only, and all four sit above the 2200 kg heaviest hand-tetherable piece.

checks.statement: Twelve upgrade purchases: six parts, two tiers each, tier 2 dearer than tier 1, each tier improving the stat it names.
checks.evidence: 12 entries, 6 parts x 2 tiers: fuel_tank 450/1150, thruster 600/1500, storage 700/1800, heat_shield 500/1300, parachute 550/1400, hand_magnet 400/1000 — tier 2 dearer in all six. Stats improve monotonically off base: fuel_capacity_kg 1800 -> 2300 -> 2900; thrust_n 78000 -> 92000 -> 108000; base_slots 6 -> 8 -> 10; plate_capacity_pct 100 -> 140 -> 190; parachute_area_m2 870 -> 1180 -> 1500; magnet_hold_force_n 900 -> 1400 -> 2000. The six parts are exactly the reduced set GDD 4.1 scopes for the semester.

checks.statement: Every band the shipping slice needs — suborbital and low — is reachable, and the catalog populates both with at least one fragile piece and at least two size classes.
checks.evidence: The catalog half holds: suborbital carries 2 fragile types (cracked_antenna_whip, shattered_lens_cowl) across 3 size classes (small, medium, oversized) and low carries 3 fragile types (cracked_solar_array, star_tracker_head, parabolic_dish_section) across the same 3, so the player meets crushing and fragility inside the slice. The reachability half does not: the simulator reports ascents suborbital reached = false, low reached = false, high reached = false, all three 'out of fuel before circularising' with 503.73 / 377.44 / 248.37 kg remaining (28% / 21% / 13.8% short). The params claim 2,542 m/s of ideal dv from exhaust velocity 78000/26 = 3000 m/s and mass ratio 3150/1350 = 2.333 (3000 * ln 2.333 = 2542), against roughly 1450 and 1800 m/s of orbital requirement — but the ideal rocket equation is not what the integrator spends, and gravity losses on the climb consume the margin. Fuel fraction is 1800/1350 = 1.33 where the grid's top-scoring worlds run 2.5-4.0. Every descent, ablation, landing and economy figure in this file is conditioned on an orbit the ship does not achieve.
checks.fix_hint: Raise flight.fuel_capacity_kg substantially — the fuel fraction of 1.33 is roughly half the 2.5-4.0 the reachable configs run — rather than cutting dry_mass_kg, which would break the full-hold doubling that pinned it at 1350.

checks.statement: No rule passes only because a number the design document fixes in prose was moved to meet it.
checks.evidence: Every quantity the GDD states in prose is intact: cargo.base_slots 6 ('Cargo reads 4 of 6', GDD 2.2, and the appendix's open question is posed against 6); eva.base_tether_slots 2; landing.soft_landing_ms 5; no_gear_multiplier 2 and fragile_multiplier 2; tow_fee.max_fee_fraction 0.5 and curve linear; magnet_range_screens 0.125 ('~1/8 of the screen'); cargo_damage_interval_s 3; heat_dissipation_s 5; compactor_tier 1; size-class slot costs 1/2, 2/4, 6/12. The one number that did move to make a rule pass is dry_mass_kg, 850 -> 1350, which carried full_hold_doubles_mass from about 1.16x to 2.035x — but the GDD never states a ship mass anywhere (the baseline's 1,800 kg is the Researcher's own flagged assumption, not a spec value), so dry mass is a free parameter and moving it is tuning rather than target-shifting. The measured quantity in that rule is the ratio, and the target the GDD does pin — 6 slots — was left alone. Knock-on consequences of that move are recorded in observations rather than here.

observations: The difficulty curve is inverted in flight, and this is the finding a human should read first after the ascent failure. Cheapest ablation empty is 4.6% (suborbital) / 4.0% (low) / 3.6% (high) and full hold is 13.5% / 11.7% / 10.8%; peak heat on the cheapest descent empty is 70 / 67 / 64. The high band is the cheapest and coolest return in the game at every load, against GDD 2.3.7's 'the value curve and the risk curve rise together'. The cost_curve asserts the opposite ordering (6.21 / 12.78 / 32.03) and passes its own check, so nothing in the audit's rule list catches this — the curve is indexed by skims and the inversion lives in the descent solver, which brakes higher bands deeper. Held at a fixed entry depth the ordering is correct (100 / 125 / 159.9 peak), so the heat model is not what is wrong.

The skim decision is arithmetic, not a feeling. In the high band 0.28 plate-percent separates 1 skim from 2 (32.31 vs 32.03) and 0.08 separates 0 from 1 in the low band. A player cannot perceive a third of a percent on a plate gauge, so the mechanic the GDD sells as a judgement call reads as a lookup table. Substituting the measured multipliers moves the high-band optimum from 2 to 1 and the separation to 0.33 — the stated optimal_skims.high = 2 is wrong against flight, even though the window it must land in is satisfied either way.

Skimming is dominated by a knob the design does not mention. Three skims buy 2.8% of peak heat at entry depth 0 and 1.7% at 21,500 m, costing 44-45 m/s of commit dv and 0.53 h each; entry depth alone moves high-band peak heat 159.9 -> 90.9 (43% cooler) over that same 21,500 m. Whatever the player is actually optimising, it is not skim count. The controlling quantity is the ballistic coefficient — staged 290.3 kg/m2 here against 33-133 in the grid worlds where skimming genuinely cools.

heat_index.high 138 is overstated by about 8%, not understated by 17% as the balance notes worried. Renormalised to the params' own low = 100 convention the measured indices are 80 / 100 / 127.9. Because the entry term is cubed, a 7.9% index error is a 26% error in the dominant cost of every high-band descent, and cost_curve.high would move with it.

The two ballistic coefficients in circulation describe different ships and should not be compared again without saying which. The params quote 591 kg/m2 (2747.8 kg full hold over Cd 1.5 x 3.1 m2); the sim reports 290.3, which back-solves to 1350 kg — dry, empty and fuel-less. Both sit far above the ~50 kg/m2 floor below which aerobraking cannot exist, so the mechanic is intact either way, but the reference area is held at 3.1 m2 across every heat-shield tier, which cannot be right for a plate you pay to upgrade and is the cheapest lever if the descents fly long.

The economy has no slack at either end. launch_cost 120 is exactly three cheap pieces, the top of its permitted window rather than inside it, and the full-hold parachute margin is 0.41 m/s of which storage tier 1 spends 0.37 (4.59 -> 4.96 m/s). Both pass, and both fail on the next revision that moves a mass anywhere.

fragile_value_premium 3.0 is thin once the uncrushable slot cost is charged. A fragile small occupies 2 slots forever against a solid small's 1, so the per-slot premium is 1.5x, not 3x — and the fragile piece additionally takes double reentry and landing damage. GDD 2.3.7 wants one recovered intact to reshape a run's payout; at 1.5x per slot the rational player who is not certain of a soft landing skips the glint, which wastes the mechanic.

dented_pressure_bottle at 380 kg in one crushed slot is the single piece that sets the shipping slice's 232.96 kg per slot, and therefore the piece that forced dry_mass_kg from 850 to 1350 to keep the doubling true. The base ship's mass is currently a function of one debris entry.
